take_homes: Default to one agent. Split only for different access, different dialect or different stance.
Give the synthesizer a framework, such as the strategy kernel, or it averages the views and nobody chooses.
The handoffs are where it breaks. When something goes wrong I check sources, processing and boundary, then write the lesson into the shared root instructions file.

monday.move: Run the three-retriever setup on the usage-pricing decision, with the Q2 review, the churn article and the pilot cohort data as sources. Ask for conflicts to be flagged, then write the handoff rules into the root instructions file.
monday.who: Me first, then one person from my team to try the same file
monday.when: Monday morning, before the pricing working group meeting
monday.stop_condition: If the curator drops a conflict between sources without flagging it, or if one prompt gives the same answer, I stop and use the single prompt.
monday.blocker: There is still no shared place for the context files, so the root instructions file stays on my machine.

misconception.why: The framework made the synthesizer commit where three views did not, and handoff rules in a shared file mattered more than prompt wording. I still think prompts matter, but they are not the main thing.

one_line: Good on when not to split agents and on where the handoffs break, but the same point is repeated three times and I still can't tell whether the final briefing is true.
